plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: A fragrant evergreen shrub with narrow gray-green leaves and dense spikes of small tubular flowers. It is widely cultivated in gardens and fields for essential oils, culinary use, and as a pollinator magnet.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer (June to August) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Mediterranean region, southern France, England, and cultivated worldwide in temperate climates
plants.funFact: Lavender has been used for over 2,500 years, and the name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', because Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with a large, coarse stem and a huge flower head made of yellow ray florets surrounding a dark disc of tiny florets that mature into seeds. Fields of sunflowers are at their peak in late July.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn (July to September)
plants.location: Native to North America; grown commercially in Ukraine, Russia, Argentina, France, and the United States
plants.funFact: Young sunflower buds track the sun across the sky in a behavior called heliotropism, but mature flowers stop moving and face east.

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: A hardy perennial prairie wildflower with daisy-like petals drooping around a spiky, orange-brown central cone. It thrives in full sun and attracts butterflies, bees, and finches seeking seeds.
plants.location: Native to the eastern and central United States prairies and open woodlands; widely cultivated in gardens
plants.funFact: Echinacea's name comes from the Greek 'echinos' meaning hedgehog, referring to the spiny central cone.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A striking evergreen shrub producing the largest flower head in the Protea genus, with a bowl of silky-tipped bracts surrounding a central cluster of tiny flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere it blooms in the cool winter and early spring period, with flowering extending through July.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to spring in the Southern Hemisphere (peaks around May to November)
plants.location: Fynbos region of the Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower, and it evolved to survive regular wildfires by storing energy in underground lignotubers.
